# Spike S2 runbook: Garnet on Windows

Status: runbook for the owner. Code stays on branch `spike/S2`; only `docs/spikes/S2.md` reaches main. Design source: `docs/design/35-spikes-plan.md` (row S2).

## 1. Question

Can Garnet on Windows, driven through StackExchange.Redis, run every command the cache and presence layer uses, and keep its data after a hard kill and restart?

## 2. Pass criteria (fixed before the first run; do not edit after running)

- Pass: all used commands pass; data survives restart.
- Fail: presence and cache need another Windows provider (doc 35, owner question 6); GC fan-out is unaffected.

"Used commands" means the list in step 5 of section 7. Until open items 4 and 7 are answered, a run passes only if both conditions hold (proposed reading).

## 3. Fail consequence and fallback

- Presence and cache wait until the owner names a Windows provider (doc 35, owner question 6, whose default is that they wait). The cache role is optional in doc 03, and with no cache, presence and cache degrade while GC delivery continues.
- GC fan-out does not depend on this spike. It runs on Postgres NOTIFY (DECISIONS-LOG C07). S2 runs whether or not S3 fails.
- Garnet stays a candidate, not a decision, until a pass is recorded.

## 4. Time-box

- One day (1 d), a hard stop. Count it from step 1 and record start and end clock times in the record.
- At expiry, the record is `inconclusive` and the run stops where it is.
- An extension needs the owner's approval, recorded in the record before any further work.

## 5. Prerequisites and environment

- The owner's NUC running Windows, with the .NET 10 SDK installed (CLAUDE.md).
- A scratch folder for Garnet data (see section 6).
- Record in the Method section before run 1:
  - OS build (for example from `winver` or `systeminfo`)
  - CPU model and RAM size
  - Garnet version and where it came from
  - StackExchange.Redis version (NuGet package version)
  - .NET version (from `dotnet --list-sdks` and `dotnet --list-runtimes`)
- No doc names a Garnet or StackExchange.Redis version. The owner picks and pins exact versions (open item 1).

## 6. Safety rules

- Keys, passwords and connection secrets never go in git, in the record or on the branch. Pass them through environment variables or an untracked local file.
- Garnet runs on a scratch data folder only, never on live Bazaar data. The plan states this for S4 and S25; applying it to S2 is proposed (open item 6).
- Garnet listens on loopback only, with authentication on (proposed; open item 2).
- Code and scratch files stay on `spike/S2`. Only `docs/spikes/S2.md` is merged to main.
- The time-box is a hard stop. The spike uses no cloud service and no paid key, so spend is zero.

## 7. Steps

1. Start the clock. Write the start time and the environment from section 5 into the record's Method section.
2. Install Garnet for Windows from its own install instructions into the scratch folder. Pin the version. Record the version, source and install path.
3. Start Garnet with the scratch data folder and the persistence setting from open item 3. Record the exact command line, the port (open item 2), and whether it started without errors.
4. On `spike/S2`, create a small .NET 10 console project that references the pinned StackExchange.Redis package. Connect to the loopback endpoint with `ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect`. Record success, or the exact exception.
5. Run each command the design uses. Record the command, key pattern, result and latency.
   a. SET with expiry: `ICacheProvider.SetAsync` (doc 03) takes a value and a TTL, so it maps to a string set with expiry.
   b. GET: `ICacheProvider.GetAsync` maps to a string get. Also read a missing key and record that it returns null.
   c. Projection snapshots (doc 11) use the same SET and GET path. No extra command is named.
   d. Presence deltas (doc 23) are "published on the cache provider". No doc names the command or pub/sub mechanism (open item 4). Do not run this check until the owner names it.
   e. Expiry: after a short TTL the key reads as null (proposed check; TTL length is open item 5).
6. Write a known data set of N keys with known values and TTLs longer than the run. Record N, the key names, and a checksum of the values (N is open item 5).
7. Hard kill: end the Garnet process forcibly (for example `taskkill /F /PID <pid>`). Record the PID and the time. Do not stop it gracefully. A power cut is not part of this runbook (open item 10).
8. Restart Garnet with the same command line and data folder. Record the time from start to first successful connection. No threshold is set (open item 5).
9. Read back every key from step 6. Record how many match the checksum, how many are missing and how many differ. Check that keys past their TTL have expired.
10. Repeat step 5 after the restart and record pass or fail for each command.
11. Stop the clock. Record the end time, the elapsed time and the run row (section 8). Commit the code and record on `spike/S2`.

## 8. Three runs

- Run 1 uses a fresh install. Runs 2 and 3 use the same pinned install with an empty scratch data folder (proposed; open item 7).
- Each run repeats steps 2 to 10 in full, with its own clock times and its own row.
- Measures per run: commands passed out of the total; keys matching after restart out of N; restart-to-connect time in milliseconds; command latency in milliseconds.
- For the timing measures, report the median and the spread (min to max). For the rest, record counts.
- The spike passes only if all three runs pass (proposed; open item 7).

| Run | Date | Measure | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | | commands passed; keys matched; restart ms | |
| 2 | | commands passed; keys matched; restart ms | |
| 3 | | commands passed; keys matched; restart ms | |

Median: (fill in). Spread (min to max): (fill in).

## 10. Consequence

The main session writes the DECISIONS-LOG entry, and assigns its round and C-number.

- Pass: record Garnet on Windows as the cache and presence provider for the first Windows host, with the tested versions pinned. Lift the candidate status in doc 03 (`host.provider.cache`, "Garnet only after S2"; work package 12), doc 11 (projection cache) and doc 23 (presence publishing). Unblocks 03, 11 and 23.
- Fail: record that Garnet is not used for the Windows cache role at the tested versions. Presence and cache wait for the provider the owner names (doc 35, owner question 6). The Windows cache role stays unset until then, which doc 03 allows because the role is optional. Doc 23 presence and doc 11 projections stay blocked. GC fan-out is unchanged (C07).
- Q9 fallback path: the owner names a Windows cache provider. A new DECISIONS-LOG entry records it, and a further spike may be needed before doc 03 work package 12 and the presence work proceed. The reference to "Q9" does not resolve in doc 03 (open item 8).
- Inconclusive: record no decision. Garnet stays a candidate, docs 03, 11 and 23 stay blocked, and S2 runs again only after the owner approves an extension or a new time-box.
- If a result contradicts a DECIDED item, it goes to the Conflicts section of doc 35 and is not fixed in the record.

## 11. Open questions

1. Which Garnet and StackExchange.Redis versions does the owner pin? No doc names one.
2. Which port, bind address and authentication method does Garnet use? Which install source is used?
3. Which Garnet persistence setting is needed for "data survives restart"? Doc 11 calls the cache rebuildable, so which keys must survive?
4. Presence publishes deltas "on the cache provider" (doc 23), but `ICacheProvider` in doc 03 has only set and get. Which commands or pub/sub mechanism does presence use?
5. Plan numbers missing: key count N, TTL length, restart-to-connect threshold, latency threshold, value sizes.
6. Does the scratch-only and loopback rule apply to S2? The plan names it only for S4 and S25.
7. Pass rule across runs: must all three pass? Is a fresh install needed for runs 2 and 3?
8. Conflict, not fixed: the S2 row and doc 03 cite "Q9". Doc 03 has no Q9; its questions are the KEK store and the admin CLI. The likely target is doc 35, owner question 6.
9. Conflict, not fixed: CLAUDE.md and `docs/deep-dives/Bazaar.Server.md` section 3 still name Garnet for cache and pub/sub without the candidate label (doc 35 Conflicts; doc 03 conflict 7).
10. Is a hard process kill enough, or does the owner also want a power-cut test?
